name: Screen width and height
plain: The monitor or phone screen size in CSS pixels, plus the usable area.
meaning: Identifies device model families (iPhone 390x844) and monitor setups (1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3440x1440). Safari 26 and Firefox protections spoof or round it for known scripts; Firefox RFP returns the window size.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: width, height
fields.precision: exact, except under RFP or AFP

fields.name: availWidth, availHeight
fields.range: less than width, height by taskbar size

limits.headline: Can see your screen width and height, and the usable area, in page units
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check the screen's width and height
Check the usable area, without the taskbar
cannot: Learn the true pixel count on scaled or Retina screens

story.what_it_is: The size of your monitor or phone screen in page units, plus its usable area.

marketing.name: Screen
marketing.pitch: Documents the object a page reads to learn the width and height of the user screen.

story.for_you: You never see it read. It is why a site can fit a big monitor or a small phone, and send the right layout from the start.
story.for_makers: It is one of the oldest and most common signals. Makers use it for layout and analytics. Trackers combine it with other facts to tell your device apart from similar ones.

use_cases.example: A browser game sets its canvas to fit the screen and chooses touch or mouse controls.
A site team sees that 55 percent of visitors use 1920 by 1080 and designs for it.
An ad server picks a banner size that fits the screen, and also keeps the size in a device profile.
A fraud service sees a screen size that no real device has and flags the visit as an emulator.
A store picks a layout and image sizes for phone, tablet or wide monitor.
A streaming site picks its first video quality from the screen size.

technical_bounds: Does not give physical size or PPI
iOS reports points, not pixels, so many iPhones share values
